Configure an Ollama backend

ollama_backend.Rd

Bundles connection and sampling settings into one object, passed down whole so parameters cannot drift between call sites. Drift can create context size differences between calls, defeating the prefix cache and forcing Ollama to reload the model.

Scoring reads log probabilities, which need an Ollama server at version 0.12.11 or later. measure() checks for them before a run and stops when none come back.

Usage

ollama_backend(
  model = NULL,
  ...,
  keep_alive = "24h",
  timeout = 600,
  top_logprobs = 20L,
  host = NULL,
  modalities = c("text", "image"),
  validate = TRUE
)

Arguments

model

A string giving the model name as Ollama knows it, e.g. "gemma3:27b". The full tag is required. Shorthand is refused. Omit it entirely to list what the server has installed.

...

Not used, and refused if anything reaches it. Every argument after it is name-only, so a misspelling lands here rather than being matched by position.

keep_alive

A string setting how long Ollama holds the model after a call. The default, "24h", is long because a corpus run over one model should not pay a reload between documents. A loop over several models on one machine wants a short value instead, since each one called stays resident for the whole window and the cost arrives as memory pressure rather than as an error.

timeout

A number giving the request timeout in seconds for generation calls. A cold prefill on a very long document can run minutes. Discovery and validation use their own shorter timeout. Default is 600.

top_logprobs

An integer giving the number of alternatives to return at each position. Ollama caps this at 20. Lower it only if every label reliably appears in the top-k. Default is 20.

host

A string giving the server URL. Defaults to OLLAMA_HOST or localhost. A host given with no scheme and no port takes port 11434, the way Ollama's own client reads OLLAMA_HOST.

modalities

A character vector of what the server accepts, which is text, image or both. A fact about the server rather than the model. measure() refuses a column naming something absent here, locally and before any call, because Ollama returns HTTP 200 for a field it does not recognize. Audio and video are not among them. prepare_audio() turns a recording into a transcript, and prepare_video() turns a video into frames plus a transcript when it has sound, which reach the model as text and image. Default is c("text", "image").

validate

A logical value indicating whether to contact the server and confirm model is installed. FALSE constructs blind with no network call, which is what examples, documentation builds, and constructor tests use. Default is TRUE.

Value

An object of class fathom_backend, a list of eight settings. It holds no connection, so it is cheap to build and safe to keep.

  • model is the tag calls are sent to. Recorded on the results as the model attribute, so a corpus says which model produced it.

  • host is the server address, normalized to include a scheme.

  • modalities holds what this server accepts. measure() refuses a column naming something absent here, before any call, because Ollama answers HTTP 200 to a field it does not recognize and an undeclared column would otherwise be discarded in silence.

  • top_logprobs says how many alternatives are requested at the answer position. Ollama caps this at 20. A label whose token falls outside the returned set is scored as absent, with a prob_renorm of exactly 0, so prob_other absorbs its mass, and item_report() reports how often that happened as pct_label_absent.

  • think is always FALSE, and not an argument. Reasoning is disabled on every call, because scoring reads generated position 1 and a model that reasons first puts something else there.

  • keep_alive says how long the server holds the model in memory between calls. Long enough that a corpus run does not pay reload cost.

  • timeout is the number of seconds before a single call is abandoned. A call that times out returns a failed row rather than ending the run.

  • validated says whether the constructor confirmed the model is installed. FALSE when built with validate = FALSE, which skips the check rather than failing it.

Called with no model name it prints what is installed and stops, which doubles as a way to confirm the server is running.

Omitting model

The call contacts the server, prints the models installed there, and errors. It does not return NULL or a partial object, so instrument() and measure() never receive a backend with no model attached.

Temperature and seed

Neither is exposed. Temperature is fixed at 0, where the returned probabilities are the model's unmodified posterior. Scoring reads the distribution at generated position 1 and discards the token that would have been drawn from it, so temperature rescales the logits being measured without changing what is read.

At temperature 0 there is no sampling, and identical calls return byte-identical token sequences. A seed has nothing to control.

See also

measure(), which takes the backend, and instrument(), which can probe labels against it.

Examples

ollama_backend("gemma3:27b", validate = FALSE)
#> Ollama backend
#> 
#> Model         gemma3:27b
#> Host          http://localhost:11434
#> Logprobs      top 20
#> Modalities    text, image
#> 
#> Note     Not validated. Built with validate = FALSE, so the model name has not
#>          been checked against the server.
